title: aoc25 day09 part 2 on master returns a wrong answer (4605625856, expected 1540192500): engine or solution bug?
description: On master 307f49f, examples/aoc25/run/day09.eu -t part-2 finishes in ~4.5s with 4605625856. An independent reference (compressed-grid flood fill + prefix sums) gives 1540192500, which matches PR #1273's rewritten solution; the reference and master both give 24 on the example input. The winning rectangle in master's answer (a pair of red tiles found by the reference) lies largely outside the polygon (753 compressed cells outside). Same answer with --source-prelude and EU_PREDECODE=0. v0.15.0 runs out of memory on this file, so it gives no comparison. In August (0.14) the same unchanged solution never finished (>600s), so nobody has seen its answer before. Diagnose: is the old levels/search pruning algorithm wrong (then the fix is #1273 and this closes), or does the engine/prelude evaluate it wrongly (then it is a P1 wrong-answer bug: minimise a repro, find the pass with eu dump, fix with a regression test)? Real inputs only in the gitignored examples/aoc25/inputs/ (recover from git history before cb93459a); never commit or quote them.
close_reason: Solution bug, not an engine bug; superseded by PR #1273. levels.xsect takes one interval [min-left, max-right] per y ('assuming single interval'), so concave polygons are treated as filled across notches and the search accepts rectangles that cross outside. A line-by-line Python port of from-points + find-max reproduces master's answer exactly and agrees with eu on 300/300 random synthetic polygons, so eucalypt evaluates the source correctly. Synthetic counterexample: C-shape [[0,0],[2,0],[2,1],[1,1],[1,3],[2,3],[2,4],[0,4]]: brute force 8, old solve2 12. PR #1273's rewrite gives the reference answer on the real input.

title: Design effect-constrained mutable storage, transients, or a memo combinator
description:
Owner decision 2026-11-11: put on the roadmap. Purpose: O(1) in-place update for workloads with 1e7+ indexed updates (AoC 2020 d23 cups, 2018 d9 marbles, 2020 d15, 2017 d5, 2018 d14; Intcode at scale), which no persistent structure reaches. Two candidate models to evaluate:
(a) Effect-confined mutable storage, like Haskell ST/STArray: mutable arrays (and possibly dicts) created and used only inside a { :do } / { :state } block where sequencing is explicit, frozen to an immutable value on exit; no mutable value escapes.
(b) Clojure-style transients: a persistent dict/vec converted to a transient, updated in place by a single owner, then made persistent again; needs a guarantee (runtime ownership check or type-level) that the transient is not shared or reused after update - harder under laziness, where evaluation order is not the textual order.
Design must address: laziness and thunk capture of a mutable value, GC (storage in the GC heap per the eu-oaz72.5 rule, write barriers if the generational GC needs them), the bytecode engine, type checker support, element types (primitives first or any value), and the interaction with par-* process parallelism. Gate: worth building only once per-step loop cost has been brought well below a microsecond (eu-oaz72.4 GC policy, eu-oaz72.27 strict accumulation) - measure first. Related: eu-oaz72.23 (persistent vector), eu-oaz72.21 (dict).
acceptance_criteria: Design note in docs/superpowers/plans comparing (a) effect-confined mutable storage, (b) transients and (c) memo combinator, with semantics, examples (a cups-style 1e7-update program; a stones-style discovered-state memo), GC and laziness analysis, and go/no-go gates tied to measured loop throughput; ROADMAP entry added.
notes:
2026-11-11 owner decision: third candidate folded in.
(c) memo(f) combinator: f: memo(g) caches g's results inside the function value; the mutation is invisible because f(k) always equals g(k). Target: memoisation where states are discovered during recursion (AoC 2024 d11 stones, non-enumerable search states), which a lazy self-referential dict (eu-oaz72.21, decision 3) cannot do because its key set is fixed at construction. Design points: cache storage in the GC heap (eu-oaz72.5 rule), keys as dict keys (primitives and lists of primitives), interaction with par-* (each forked worker has its own cache), re-entrancy when g recursively calls f on a thunk that is mid-evaluation, cache growth and lifetime (tied to the function value's reachability), and the bytecode engine. Pure alternatives to compare: threading a dict through recursion or { :state } (works today once dict exists; clumsy and needs strict accumulation, eu-oaz72.27), and a lazy infinite trie over the key space (MemoTrie-style; fine for ints, awkward for lists/strings, memory-heavy).
Enumerable-state memoisation needs nothing new beyond eu-oaz72.21 plus a cookbook example (eu-oaz72.16).

title: Prelude: general-purpose helpers surfaced by Advent of Code
description: Pure prelude additions repeatedly hand-written in AoC: gcd, lcm, modpow, CRT, frequencies, enumerate/map-indexed, find/index-of, combinations/permutations, str.reverse, regex all-matches-with-groups, a char-grid parser (lines -> vec + width/height + coordinate helpers, neighbours4/8), interval merge, cycle detection (find period then extrapolate), memoised fix-point helper (once a map exists). Some may belong in an optional `aoc`/`grid` library rather than the prelude - owner decision.
acceptance_criteria: Agreed list implemented with docs, types and tests; used in the AoC cookbook.
notes:
2026-11-11 owner direction: AoC-specific helpers (str.ints, grid parsing, neighbour helpers, cycle detection and similar) go in a separate AoC helper library kept with the AoC solutions, not in the prelude. Prelude candidates stay general-purpose: str.matches-with(re) (all matches, each as [whole, g1, ...], i.e. matches-of(re) map(match-with(re)); name chosen to pair with match-with, document beside matches-of), gcd, lcm, modpow, frequencies, enumerate, find/index-of, combinations/permutations, str.reverse, interval merge.
2026-11-12: frequencies(xs) returns a dict (eu-oaz72.21) once dict exists, not a block.
2026-11-12: modpow and CRT moved to eu-oaz72.24 (need i128 internally).
2026-11-14 (coordinator): candidate helpers that the AoC cookbook (#1216) writes inline: gcd/lcm, str-drop, run-until, interval merge, ints. Weigh them against the plan's §6 list; names still need fixing in advance for agent merge.
Design (str.matches-with): matches-with(re, s): matches-of(re, s) map(match-with(re)); type string -> string -> [[string]]; all matches each as [whole, g1..]; documented beside matches-of; harness test in tests/harness/. Only this helper in PR #1; other candidates proposed below.
PROPOSED (not implemented; for owner decision). Recommend adding all in prelude unless marked:
- gcd(a, b): number->number->number, Euclid on integers; gcd(0,b)=|b|. lcm(a, b): |a*b|/gcd, lcm(0,_)=0. Recommend yes.
- frequencies(xs): [a]->dict count per distinct element (dict from eu-oaz72.21); wait for dict.
- enumerate(xs): [a]->[[number,a]] pairs from 0 (i.e. zip(range(0,count(xs)), xs)); recommend yes (0-based).
- find(p, xs): first element satisfying p, else error?? Recommend find-or(d,p,xs)-style: find(p,xs) returns element or null; index-of(x, xs): first 0-based index or null. Recommend yes, null on miss.
- combinations(n, xs): [[a]] all n-element subsequences in input order; permutations(xs): [[a]] all orderings, lexicographic by input position. Recommend yes, lazy lists.
- str.reverse(s): string->string, reverses by character. Recommend yes.
- merge-intervals(is): [[number,number]]->same, sorted, overlapping/touching merged (inclusive ends). Recommend yes.
- AoC-specific (ints, grid, neighbours, cycle detection): AoC library, not prelude (owner 2026-11-11).
PR #1244 sent back in round 1 by both independent reviewers: context-sensitive regexes (\B, ^, $) give wrong groups under the owner-fixed definition. Owner decisions: eu-oaz72.163 / eu-oaz72.164 (duplicates). Mechanical findings fixed.
str.matches-with shipped in PR #1244 as option B (decision 38; record on eu-oaz72.164). The other helpers (gcd, lcm, frequencies, enumerate, find, index-of, combinations, permutations, str.reverse, merge-intervals) wait for the owner's answer on names.
2026-11-17 owner decision 43 (first-hand): names and behaviours fixed - gcd(a,b), lcm(a,b) (integers; gcd(0,b)=|b|, lcm(0,_)=0; non-integer is an error naming the function), frequencies(xs) (dict of counts), enumerate(xs) ([[i,x]], 0-based), find(p,xs) (first match or null), index-of(x,xs) (0-based index or null), combinations(n,xs) and permutations(xs) (lazy, input order), str.reverse(s) (by character as str.letters splits), merge-intervals(is).
2026-11-17 owner decision 46 (first-hand): merge-intervals takes closed integer intervals; sorted [lo1,hi1],[lo2,hi2] merge when lo2 <= hi1 + 1 (adjacent merge: [1,3]+[4,6] give [1,6]; [1,3]+[5,6] stay separate); non-integer bounds are an error naming the function.
Implemented in PR #1258 (all prelude, no intrinsics).

title: Lazy foldl retains the list it walks: flat (capture-trimmed) thunks plus selector thunks
description:
Split from eu-oaz72.175. With closed-binding (eu-oaz72.175's fix) count, foldl-strict and wrapper shapes run in constant space, but lazy foldl still retains the list: its accumulator thunk op(i, l head) is not forced until the end, and each thunk's env is the whole iteration frame (op, i, l), so the 200k-thunk chain holds every cell, including the dead slot l. Measured-single, 200k cells, closed-binding applied: foldl-strict 1,026 peak blocks, count 1,026, foldl 11,001, list-free lazy chain 3,513. Diagnosis: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-17-foldl-retention.md on branch eu-oaz72.175/foldl-trace.

A fix needs both flat (capture-trimmed) thunks, which owner decision 33 declined for now, and a selector-thunk rule (head/tail of an already-evaluated local cons becomes an alias of the field). Flat thunks change the blob wire format (capture list in the form header). Medium-large; sensitive-area review. The lazy chain is O(n) by design (decision 31 kept foldl's lazy accumulator; foldl-strict is the constant-space form), so this only removes the extra list retention. Owner decision needed before any work.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Coordinator: both parts are required together; neither alone fixes it. Flat thunks alone: the accumulator thunk op(i, l head) still needs l, and l is the cons cell that leads to the rest of the list. Selector rule alone: l head becomes the element, but the thunk still captures the whole frame, which holds l. Together the thunk captures only the element, i and op. The wire-format change comes with flat thunks; the selector rule alone needs none. Neither part has been prototyped.

title: Design arbitrary-precision integers (bignum) for eucalypt
description: Owner decision 2026-11-12: roadmap design item. Today numbers are serde_json::Number (i64/u64/f64): + and * error on overflow, ^ will error too (eu-oaz72.12). Modular cases are covered by eu-oaz72.24 (mulmod/powmod/modinv in i128). Remaining need: exact arithmetic beyond 64 bits for linear algebra and rationals on large values (AoC 2023 d24 p2 cross products ~1e29, 2022 d21 p2 solving through divisions), where f64 rounding gives wrong answers. Design questions: automatic promotion on overflow (Python semantics) vs an explicit bigint type; whether to add exact rationals; storage of digits in the GC heap (no Rust Vec/BigInt allocations inside heap objects, per the eu-oaz72.5 rule) or inline small/large split; arithmetic, comparison, hashing/ordering (dict keys, eu-oaz72.21), rendering (YAML/JSON refuse values above i64 today), type checker; performance impact on the common i64 path (must be negligible); replacing serde_json::Number as the core number type.
acceptance_criteria: Design note in docs/superpowers/plans with a recommendation, semantics, storage layout under the GC-heap rule, rendering rules, and a measured plan for zero regression on i64 arithmetic; ROADMAP entry added.

title: Tree-sitter grammar mis-parses juxtaposed list-parameter definitions and chained multi-argument calls
